title: Cradleward - Idle, Mobile First, Space Trading (pre-alpha)
author: jaofos
selftext:
I'm in the prototype stage of making a game that I would want to play.  I love space games, but between the family and full time job, I can't make the committment to the games I love like Eve Online, Elite Dangerous, X4 Foundations, so I'm making my own damn game, with hookers, and blow.  (but not really)

The premise is a slow paced, async interaction world that is idle / mobile friendly.  Space ships, gate camps, trading, mining, building in a player driven universe is the end goal.

This is not that, this is a prototype, playtesting pacing, functionality, "how does it feel?", turning the knobs as I build out features in my spare time.

I'd like to share this project, get some feedback, input, collaboration.  What works, what doesn't?  Right now it's just a static web site, runs on your machine, no servers (which means no moving your save to a new browser).

Let me know what you think.

[https://alpha.cradleward.com](https://alpha.cradleward.com)

comments.author: askchris
comments.body: I like the idea, but it took literally 3-5 minutes to move a few pixels. Sure, I should be more patient since I'm traveling light-years across the void which could take literally hundreds of years in real life, but for a game it lost my patience. I also would tap on a hex grid location and scan my eyes down to the info box and then scan back to understand where I'm looking -- basically the info box that tells you what you clicked on could have been more integrated with the map (I'm thinking a way point). Also it wasn't immediately clear what I'm supposed to do: the first thing I did when I started the game was pinch to zoom into the map, then tapped around the map but got bored waiting for my ship to do anything useful. I did see there's a bunch of ore prices at my destination but that also felt uninteresting to me ... Not sure what to "improve" but that's where these games usually lose my attention.

replies.author: jaofos
replies.body:
Thanks for the reply!  I definitely have the game purposefully tuned to be slow right now.   If you want to rush through you can add ?speed=10 to the url to increase the pacing.  

Right now the early game consists of exploring the universe to identify ports and trade routes, start running goods between ports to buy modules, a new ship and a second / third clone which lets you run multiple ships and missions simultaneously. 

Long term plans for careers in the game is dedicated explorer (a ship that can find hidden asteroid belts and pirate sites to run), combat both PvE and PvP, mining, player structures and raids into the center of the universe.

replies.author: askchris
replies.body: Oh fast response! I just edited my review above a second ago, added some more insights to help.

replies.author: jaofos
replies.body: There is some initial info into the lore and why on cradleward.com.  I’m building out the careers , ships and things you actually get to interact with first then I’ll sprinkle in the lore through quests , missions and some onboarding.

replies.author: askchris
replies.body:
I tried it with speed=10 and it's way more playable -- Maybe that should be the default speed?

Just realized if we can pick our ship at the beginning that could take care of some onboarding since we might commit more to the game (what I customize, I feel like I own) -- choosing a ship could feel like choosing a personality or goal, since it would allow us to subtly "choose our intent" (hauler vs miner vs mercenary etc) which also suits the players mood or goals or personality -- this also unconsciously sets the tone and focus for the player, it gives them an identity and a why.

Thoughts?

replies.author: jaofos
replies.body:
I think it’s great feedback.  My start was kind of modeled after Eve Online, you get a starter ship and slowly work your way into what you want to do by discovering the universe. You can train a little ways into a lot of things before dedicating to a speciality.  The game definitely opens up when you get your second clone.  

My thought process may be a bit extreme , but I was trying to avoid someone exploring the entire universe on day one and getting board. The pace is that it should take you a month in real life to fully explore the galaxy.  

For early testing I’ll adjust that tomorrow when I dive back into updates.  Increase the pace, some explanations and onboarding on first open.  The career path right now is kind of stuck at trading until I get mining and combat implemented.

replies.author: askchris
replies.body:
Makes sense ... Hoping the player will want to take a month to explore the Galaxy means their motivation and commitment to the game needs to be very high, and the Galaxy needs to feel "worth it" so getting the first few minutes right (emotionally) will probably enable that. 

So I guess this game is (currently) for people who already want to trade in a universe, but for me trading feels like grinding without a purpose behind it. 

For example if the mysterious aliens are destroying my fellow human settlements at the galactic rim, and my family's colony could be attacked next... Then I might feel the desire to make a difference somehow, upgrade my ship and/or build a fleet to face these aliens, (or whatever plot) then I might want to trade and mine in order to build up my ship and fleet. I'm sure there are better plot mechanics but something like this would be more engaging for me... 

For my personality I'm more of a casual explorer type, so making it feel fun to explore would be the way to pull someone like me into the game. 

I've always wanted to make an open space exploration game (I loved Star Control 2). I also like those simple territory take over type games.

I'm hoping your game succeeds because I also want to make games like this that succeed. 

It's also cool to see you're targetinh yourself by asking "what would I actually enjoy playing"? 

And I think you're doing that so let's see if you can attract similar people who feel the same as you about space games.

replies.author: jaofos
replies.body: For sure.  That is all coming as the bottleneck is between my brain and the keyboard.  The premise of the story is that there is a "Swarm" of AI enemies protecting the cradle at the center of the universe.  The cradle is the source of cloning tech and vast resources and riches, that the swarm guard heavily.  The swarm has begun to push into the rim of the galaxy where humanity has settled.  It will take coordination to break through the gates and reach the cradle.. for.. what, I don't know yet :)

comments.author: oadephon
comments.body:
Man, you need some tutorialization. Invite the player in, hold their hand for a minute. 

I couldn't tell where to go or what to do, I eventually went to a place, but it looks like I can't buy anything from there until I visit another place that I can sell it to? It's like, minutes of gameplay where you aren't actually able to interact with the game world beyond sending your ship, unless I'm missing something.

replies.author: jaofos
replies.body:
Very fair. I am inviting everyone in pretty raw.  
 This is pre-alpha so it’s nowhere near what it will become over the next few weeks.  I probably should have prioritized onboarding before sharing, but I’ve been enjoying it enough I thought I could get some early feedback.  

I’ve never made a game, nor sold a product, I’m just a dude in his basement after work trying to make something fun.

replies.author: jaofos
replies.body: Give it another go, I think I made some good improvements around this aspect.

comments.author: jaofos
comments.body:
Thanks for the initial feedback.  Made some adjustments that will help with the pacing given the state of things.

\- Increased the pacing 10x (time estimates will be wrong for now)  
\- Added a brief intro to the universe at the start  
\- New sprite renders that point ships in the correct direction as they travel  
\- "Follow" mode follows your ship around as you fly  
\- Tutorial cards that give you milestones to start (find your first port, explore the home system), at the end you'll have enough credits to buy a second clone + a ship of your choice  
\- Increased the orders queue size from 1 to 4

comments.author: jaofos
comments.body:
# Cradleward — What's New Today

# Field operations

* Ships now carry a hold, and cargo stays aboard when a run is broken off
* **DRILL** runs as a standing operation on a seam — set it once and it works the rock
* **COLLECT** is the hauler's half: send a second hull to lift what the drill has pulled
* Operations are discoverable — find someone working a field and join it
* A laden hull runs louder, and is easier to catch

# The skill tree

* Full skill tree, drawn as a tree, with a lens per career
* Engrams for sale at the home academy — each one a sealed card until you have the standing for it
* New skills: Underwriting, Portage, Drill Rigging
* Command skills now key what your clone can captain

# Shipyards

* 24 hull casts, each yard building to its own philosophy
* Shipyard headquarters stand on the contested ring
* Standing with a yard is earned in the field, and unlocks what its showroom will sell you

# Hunting

* Patrols are flown for real, and a kill has a place on the map
* Bounties are local — a hunt is somebody's problem, posted where the trouble is
* Dispatch a hunt from wherever your hull rests, not just from port

# Interface

* Every dropdown is gone. Choices are now visible lists, chips, or checkboxes
* Sell targets show the real per-hour value of each destination before you commit
* The mining form asks one question — the drill runs until the hold is full
* Selecting a hex raises its answer beside it, and navigation commits right there on the map

# Map

* Stations and shipyards draw as towers instead of diamonds
* Seams show their mineral in the silhouette and their prospecting in the light
* Ships turn to face where they're flying; gate jumps get a beam and a landing
* Standing orders draw their planned route before it flies
* Discovered shipyards appear on the universe map

# Getting started

* A welcome for new commanders, and a briefing chain that teaches as you go
* Seven-rung milestone ladder riding the map, each rung explaining its task and paying out on completion

# Also

* Break off a mission in flight — DUMP & FLY, DIVERT, or a NOW option beside every queued order
* FOLLOW turns the clone card into a chase camera that crosses gates with your hull
* Prospect park and field book — price a rock before you commit a barge
* Every clone you decant gets a name you choose
* Surveying and sweeping merged into one **RE-SURVEY**
* Pre-alpha runs the clock at 10x, offline time included
